headline: DART reports improved easy-to-hard accuracy for recurrent reasoning models
summary: An arXiv preprint introduces Distributional Adversarial Recurrent Training (DART), which trains recurrent reasoning models with a locally perturbed target distribution and an input-conditioned adversarial critic. The authors report improved easy-to-hard results for Deep Thinking Systems on mazes and chess puzzles and for Tiny Recursive Models on masked Sudoku. For 31×31 mazes, reported accuracy is 99.91±0.13% with DART versus 73.92±26.01% with cross-entropy; at 50% Sudoku masking and depth 56, reported accuracy is 38.0±0.1% versus 32.4±1.7%. Chess still shows late-iteration degradation with DART alone; combining it with progressive training is reported to improve final accuracy. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced here.
